choice.description: Will the inspection sample contain at least one defective unit (so that lot PSU-2609-07 is rejected)? Give probabilities that reflect the evidence in the state. Rubric — false: None of the sampled units is defective.; true: At least one of the sampled units is defective..

contexts:
KORRIDAN ELECTRONICS — INCOMING INSPECTION, LOT PSU-2609-07 (12 POWER SUPPLY UNITS)

Supplier certificate: the supplier's own end-of-line test found that exactly 3 of the 12 units in this lot are defective (output ripple above specification). The defective units were not marked and are indistinguishable from good units without testing. Korridan has verified that the supplier's count is exact.

Sampling plan SP-4 (version 2): the inspector draws 2 units at random, without replacement, and tests them.
Sampling plan SP-4 (version 3, in force from 1 September 2026, supersedes version 2): the inspector draws 3 units at random, without replacement, and tests them. The lot is rejected if any tested unit is defective.

Other lots received the same day (for information): PSU-2609-05 (20 units, supplier reports 0 defective, accepted after sampling), PSU-2609-06 (8 units, supplier reports 1 defective, sampling pending).
Test procedure: each sampled unit is load-tested for 15 minutes; a unit whose ripple exceeds specification is classified defective. The test is assumed to be perfectly accurate for this purpose.
Inspection date: 18 September 2026. The inspector follows the plan in force. No unit has been tested yet.
Inspector's note: "With a quarter of the lot defective, chance of catching one is under 50% — probably passes."
